title: Lifting a bounded-above acyclic complex through an ideal
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, let $I \subset R$ be an ideal, and let $\mathcal{P}$ be a class of $R$-modules. Assume: (1) every $P \in \mathcal{P}$ is projective; (2) if $P_1 \in \mathcal{P}$ and $P_1 \oplus P_2 \in \mathcal{P}$, then $P_2 \in \mathcal{P}$; and (3) every map $P_1 \to P_2$ between members of $\mathcal{P}$ that is surjective modulo $I$ is surjective. If $E^\bullet$ is a bounded-above acyclic complex of $R/I$-modules [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] whose terms are each isomorphic to $P/IP$ for some $P \in \mathcal{P}$, then there exists a bounded-above acyclic complex $A^\bullet$ with all terms in $\mathcal{P}$ and an isomorphism $A^\bullet/IA^\bullet \cong E^\bullet$ of complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules].
